decision: Scheduler auto-fire is dual-mechanism: synchronous post-persist hook in scripts/run_backtest.py + hourly safety-net reconciler in src/scheduler/watch.py. Both write to a shared auto_fire_walkforward helper in src/platform/walkforward_autofire.py (NEW file). Per-strategy concurrency via filelock at data/walkforward-{strategy_id}.lock. Max 3 attempts per (strategy_id, code_git_sha) per 24h. Behind WALKFORWARD_AUTOFIRE_ENABLED env var (default true). Auto-fire failures emit platform_events rows but NEVER raise — a backtest persist success must not be voided by an auto-fire failure.
rationale: Post-persist hook provides zero-latency trigger at source-of-truth (operator runs run_backtest.py and expects same-day walkforward). Hourly reconciler closes the gap when parent process crashes after persist. Both mechanisms share a helper to unify failure handling. filelock prevents two backtests racing on the same strategy. The 3-attempt cap prevents runaway retry loops; platform_events provides full audit trail. Sentinel discipline matches SP-WF-009 (default-true, escape-hatch off).
alternatives_considered: Pure scheduler-tick polling (rejected — adds 60-min latency; operator expects same-day result)
Event-bus pub/sub (rejected — YAGNI; platform_events is the only existing audit trail, no need for new abstraction)
Synchronous in-process walkforward call (rejected — would block scripts/run_backtest.py for 10-60 min, breaking CLI ergonomics)
Single mechanism (post-persist hook only, no reconciler — rejected; leaves a gap when parent process crashes)
source: operator-interview (BRIEF requirement: scheduler auto-fire closes manual-CLI gap) + codebase-constraint (watch.py:2176 _run_postclose_reconciliation pattern + scripts/run_backtest.py:94 persist call site) + v1-spec-reference (SP-WF-009 sentinel discipline pattern + SP-WF-010 corpus binding)

decision: _evaluate_production_gate is extended to call _evaluate_walkforward_gate symmetrically with _evaluate_shadow_trading_gate. Composition: passes_dsr AND walkforward_pass AND methodology_pass. Honors the same WALKFORWARD_GATE_ENABLED sentinel from T9 (one sentinel, both gates). Stricter no-row policy: if walkforward gate returns (None, evidence), production gate returns False (NOT legacy fall-through that shadow_trading uses). PBO production-gate wiring stays explicitly out of scope — line 519 (evidence['pbo'] = None) stays; T14 only closes line 520's walkforward placeholder.
rationale: Symmetry with _evaluate_shadow_trading_gate is the simplest design and aligns with v1 spec SP-WF-008 (AND-composition at orchestrator level, not voter). Stricter no-row policy reflects the lifecycle invariant: any strategy reaching production has already passed shadow_trading, which required a walkforward row — so a production attempt with no walkforward row indicates a manual override or a broken lifecycle, both blocking. Single sentinel is operationally simpler — if operator wants to bypass walkforward for production specifically, they bypass for both.
alternatives_considered: Legacy fall-through symmetric with shadow_trading (rejected — production is higher-stakes; we choose conservatism over symmetry with legacy fall-through)
New sentinel PRODUCTION_WALKFORWARD_GATE_ENABLED (rejected — duplicates SP-WF-009; one sentinel for both gates is simpler)
Wire PBO production-gate in same task (rejected — scope creep; PBO has its own decision history and is explicitly deferred)
Make _evaluate_production_gate call check_promotion_gate(target='shadow_trading') internally (rejected — recursive semantics and would re-run methodology gate twice)

decision: Three production-detectable SQL queries documented in docs/operator-guide.md (added by T15) prove or disprove the T13+T14 wiring: (1) orphan-backtest query — finds backtest_results rows older than 2h without a paired walkforward_results row (T13 falsifier); (2) production-promotion-walkforward-evidence query — finds strategy_promotion_events with to_status='production' lacking walkforward_outcome_state in gate_result_json (T14 falsifier); (3) auto-fire-failure-rate query — counts platform_events with event_type LIKE 'walkforward_auto_fire%' in the last 7 days (T13 systemic-failure detector). Expected thresholds: query 1 zero rows after reconciler runs; query 2 zero rows post-Sprint-6; query 3 < 5% of total auto-fires.
rationale: Silent-failure modes for scheduler triggers are the highest-risk class — they pass tests in worktree (where the trigger fires synchronously) but fail in production (where the child process dies post-fork). Operator memory 'feedback_worktree_env_drift' documents PR #711→#729 incident where worktree-green tests 401'd post-merge. T13's child-process spawn is especially susceptible. Three SQL queries with concrete thresholds let the operator detect drift without reading code — directly addressable in the operator-guide.md and in the watch-loop weekly digest. Production-detectability is the falsifiability discipline CLAUDE.md memory 'feedback_review_sibling_search' enforces.
alternatives_considered: Heartbeat/health-check HTTP endpoint (rejected — heavier than three SQL queries an operator can paste into REPL; would require new route + frontend surfacing)
Telegram alert on auto-fire failure (rejected — out of Sprint 6 scope; requires notification routing layer changes)
Do not document falsifiability (rejected — operator memory feedback_review_sibling_search requires falsifiability claims be testable)
Embed falsifiability checks as pytest tests only (rejected — pytest runs in CI, not in production; production-detectability is the goal here)

decision: Sentinel-consistency check at startup. When WALKFORWARD_GATE_ENABLED=true AND WALKFORWARD_AUTOFIRE_ENABLED=false (asymmetric configuration), `python -m src.main startup` emits a warning to Telegram + log. ALSO: when `_evaluate_walkforward_gate` returns `passes=False` due to no-row, the evidence dict includes `auto_fire_enabled` so the operator sees both pieces of state at gate-reject time.
rationale: Devil's Advocate DA-6 surfaced a sentinel-combination deadlock: GATE=true + AUTOFIRE=false creates a hard-stop on promotion attempts (gate requires walkforward rows that auto-fire would have produced). Spec v1.0 mentioned the combination casually ('manual CLI still works') but never surfaced the operational risk. Startup-time warning gives the operator immediate visibility; evidence-dict inclusion makes the gate-reject diagnostic explicit.
alternatives: Couple the two flags: setting GATE=true auto-implies AUTOFIRE=true (rejected — removes operator override flexibility)
Silent / log-only warning (rejected — Telegram channel ensures operator sees it)
Block startup on asymmetric config (rejected — too aggressive; operator may have legitimate reasons)
